explanation: Search the b-dimensional bit cube from zero. Try flipping each bit of the last code; append only an unseen result and backtrack if it cannot complete the sequence. At full length, also test that the last and first code differ by one bit.
timeComplexity: O(b·b^(2^b)) conservative backtracking bound: depth is at most 2^b, each node tries b bit flips and set operations. The observed first successful path is often much shorter; a direct-formula linear bound does not describe this implementation. Formula variants perform constant word operations per one of 2^b outputs; search variants have the separately stated branching bound.
spaceComplexity: O(2^b) auxiliary space for visited codes and recursion depth, plus O(2^b) output. Formula variants retain only loop state beyond output; search retains its history and path stack.

correctness: The history set equals the current path and prevents repeated codes. Every extension changes exactly one bit, so any full path has all 2^b distinct b-bit values with valid neighbors. The final check additionally closes the cycle. Trying every unused one-bit neighbor is complete for this search. For b>0 the reflected sequence also closes cyclically: its last value is 1<<(b-1), one bit from zero. The bank adapter only requires consecutive output pairs.
walkthrough: For b=3, low-bit-first extensions visit 0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4. Each XOR of adjacent values has one set bit; 4 XOR 0 also has one bit. Return the sequence; the bank wrapper reports true after validating it.
edgeCases: Zero bits gives the single value [0].
Do not repeat a pattern or use values outside the b-bit range.
The output has exponential size even though each value is computed in constant word operations.
